result.topic_en: Derivation of the jump (shock) conditions for a one-dimensional gas flow with isothermal pressure law, using conservation of mass and momentum across a discontinuity moving at speed dξ/dt, and their relation to the Riemann invariants p = log ρ + u/a, q = log ρ − u/a.
result.transcription:
[diagram: axes with a line from the origin, labelled $0$]

$\varrho, u \quad x, t.$ \quad $x = \xi - 0 \quad x = \xi + 0$
$\varrho_1 \quad \varrho_2$
$u_1 \quad u_2$

$[-u_1-] \frac{\partial\xi}{\partial t} = v_1 \quad u_2 - \frac{\partial\xi}{\partial t} = v_2$
$v_1\varrho_1\omega\partial t = v_2\varrho_2\omega\partial t$
$(v_2 - v_1)[-\varrho_1-]\varrho_1 v_1 \omega\partial t = aa(\varrho_1 - \varrho_2)\omega\partial t$

$v_1\varrho_1 = v_2\varrho_2$
$\left(\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2} - 1\right) v_1^2\varrho_1 = aa\,\varrho_1 - \varrho_2 \qquad v_1 = \pm a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}}$
$v_1^2 = aa\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1} \quad v_2^2 = aa\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2} \qquad v_2 = \pm a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$

$\frac{\partial\xi}{\partial t} = u_1 + a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}} = [-\frac{\partial\xi}{\partial t}-]u_2 + a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$
$= u_1 - a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_2}{\varrho_1}} = u_2 - a\sqrt{\frac{\varrho_1}{\varrho_2}}$

$\frac{\partial p}{\partial t} = -(u+a)\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}$
$\frac{\partial q}{\partial t} = -(u-a)\frac{\partial q}{\partial x}$
$p = \log\varrho + \frac{u}{a} \quad u+a$
$q = \log\varrho - \frac{u}{a}$

[sketch: profile with a jump]
[sketch: profile with a jump]

$\varrho_1 > \varrho_2$
$u_1 + a > \frac{\partial\xi}{\partial t} > u_2 + a$

$p_1 \quad p_2 \quad q_2 \qquad [-u_2-u_1-] \quad [-\Delta p-]$

$\Delta p = \Delta\log\varrho + \frac{\Delta u}{a}$

$\frac{\Delta u}{a} = e^{\frac{1}{2}\Delta\log\varrho} - e^{-\frac{1}{2}\Delta\log\varrho} = \Delta\log\varrho - \Delta p$

methods.what: Relative velocities of fluid with respect to the moving discontinuity
Momentum conservation across the shock with isothermal pressure $a^2\varrho$
Solution for relative velocities in terms of density ratio
Shock speed expressed from both sides
Riemann invariants and their transport equations for isothermal gas
Shock inequality (Lax-type entropy condition) for compressive shock
Jump of the Riemann invariant p across the shock
Velocity jump as function of log-density jump (hyperbolic-sine relation)

items.english: If ρ1 > ρ2, then u1 + a > dξ/dt > u2 + a.
